Which of the following taxes is/are an example (s) of the Indirect taxes?

I. Gift tax

II. Excise duty

III. securities transaction tax

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.solution_en:
A tax is a legal compulsory payment by the people and firms to the government of a country without reference to any direct benefits in return. All taxes are of two kinds:

i) Direct taxes

ii) Indirect Taxes.

In the case of direct taxes, the liability of payment and the burden of the tax falls on the same person. For example, income tax is a direct tax because the person who is liable to pay it also bears the burden of the tax; The burden of the tax cannot be shifted on others. Others are wealth tax, corporate tax, gift tax.

The Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied in India on transactions done on the domestic stock exchanges. It is categorised as a direct tax.

In the case of indirect taxes, the burden of tax is shifted from the seller to the buyer. For example, in Goods and services tax liability to pay tax lies with the seller of a good the actual burden of the tax falls on the buyer. All taxes on production are indirect taxes because producers recover these taxes from buyers by increasing the price of the product. Other examples are Excise duty (the tax on goods manufactured in factories), Customs duty (tax on imports and exports).

Consider the below statements on mitochondria and endosymbiosis.

Statement 1: Mitochondria possess circular DNA and can replicate semi-autonomously within eukaryotic cells.

Statement 2: This is because mitochondria evolved from aerobic bacteria via endosymbiosis.

questions.solution_en:
Both statements 1 and 2 are true, and statement 2 is the correct explanation for the observations described in statement 1. The prokaryotic origin of mitochondria explains why they possess features like circular DNA and the ability to replicate semi-autonomously. Therefore, the correct option is a.

Explanation of Statements:

Statement 1 is True. Mitochondria contain their own small, circular chromosome (mtDNA), separate from the nuclear DNA of the cell. They also have their own ribosomes and can replicate through a process similar to binary fission. However, they are only "semi-autonomous" because they rely on proteins encoded by the cell's nuclear DNA to function and replicate.

Statement 2 is True. The endosymbiotic theory is the leading explanation for the origin of mitochondria. It posits that an ancestral host cell engulfed an aerobic bacterium. Instead of being digested, the bacterium established a symbiotic relationship, eventually evolving into the mitochondrion.

Statement 2 explains Statement 1. The reason mitochondria have bacteria-like features (circular DNA, semi-autonomous replication) is a direct consequence of their evolutionary origin from a free-living bacterium, as described by the endosymbiotic theory.

Further Insights:

Other evidence supporting the endosymbiotic theory includes the fact that mitochondria have a double membrane (the inner membrane corresponding to the original bacterial membrane and the outer one from the host cell's vesicle) and have ribosomes that are more similar to prokaryotic ribosomes than eukaryotic ones.

A similar process is believed to have led to the evolution of chloroplasts in plant cells from an engulfed cyanobacterium.

Consider the statements below with respect to the reaction given here:

An iron nail is dipped into a blue CuSO4 solution; a reddish-brown deposit forms and the solution's color fades to green.

i. This is a single displacement reaction.

ii. Copper is more reactive than iron.

iii. The solution turns green due to FeSO₄ formation.

Which of the above statement is/are true?
questions.solution_en:
Statements i and iii are correct.

Statement ii is incorrect because in this displacement reaction, iron displaces copper, which proves that iron is more reactive than copper. Therefore, the correct option is c.

Explanation of Statements:

i is Correct. The reaction, Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s), is a classic example of a single displacement reaction. Here, a more reactive element (iron) displaces a less reactive element (copper) from its salt solution.

ii is Incorrect. The reactivity series of metals dictates which element can displace another. Since iron successfully displaces copper from the solution, it demonstrates that iron is more reactive than copper, not the other way around. The reddish-brown deposit is the less reactive copper metal precipitating out of the solution.

iii is Correct. The initial blue color of the solution is due to the presence of hydrated copper(II) ions (Cu⁺). As the reaction proceeds, these are replaced by iron(II) ions (Fe⁺) from the newly formed iron(II) sulfate (FeSO₄). Aqueous solutions containing Fe⁺ ions are typically pale green.

Further Insights:

This experiment is a common way to demonstrate the relative positions of iron and copper in the reactivity series.

The underlying principle is electrochemical. Iron is more easily oxidized (loses electrons) than copper, so it readily gives up electrons to copper ions, reducing them to copper metal while the iron itself becomes an ion in the solution.

questions.q_en: What is the function of Gibberellins in plants?
questions.solution_en: Gibberellins (GAs) are plant hormones that regulate growth and influence various developmental processes, including stem elongation, germination, dormancy, flowering, sex expression, enzyme induction, and leaf and fruit senescence. Gibberellins play an important role in several developmental stages in plants, but their claim to fame is making stems longer. Gibberellins promote stem elongation between nodes on the stem. A node is a place on a stem where a leaf attaches, so gibberellins elongate the internodes. It is easiest to see the absence of gibberellin in dwarf plants and rosette plants - there is very little space between nodes on a stem and the leaves are clustered toward the base of the plant.
